comparison: Same public practice tasks, prerequisite gates, action menus, approved questions, evidence, UI and time budget. Only action selection differs: local model versus first allowed scaffold action. Model fallbacks remain in their assigned arm and are reported.
design: Researcher-assigned counterbalanced forms: pretest A/posttest B or pretest B/posttest A; block randomize coaching arm and form order. Forms are provisional and must be difficulty-calibrated before confirmatory use.
primary: Intention-to-treat mean proportion of three trained-family posttest tasks passing every private target and control case, adjusted for corresponding pretest score and form order. Missing posttest tasks count as not passed; report available-case sensitivity and infrastructure failures separately.
exploratory: Unpractised-family tasks, regression quality, explanation quality, wall-clock time, hint requests, model fallbacks and action distributions. Do not call unpractised tasks proven far transfer.
analysis: Do not infer learner effects from model decisions, reference repairs or simulated learner records. Freeze sample size and analysis before recruitment after feasibility and power planning; no sample size or positive effect is assumed here. Report arm counts, attrition, intervals, fallback rate and form effects. Preserve randomized arm for intention-to-treat analysis.
contamination: Original synthetic assessment tasks authored for this development run, excluded from mentor prompts and public practice catalog. Designers and code reviewers can inspect answers; generic mechanisms may be known to models. Publishing source exposes the bank. Held out from practice/prompt tuning does not mean guaranteed unseen, private forever or tamper-proof.
privacy: Assessment UI keeps source, reasoning and exports on the learner device. Offline grading is operator-run. No learner telemetry, recruitment messages or real outcome dataset is created by this milestone.
integrity: Same-origin mentor calls are blocked during an active assessment, including relabelled task IDs. External tools, edited exports, other browser profiles and operator access cannot be ruled out; unaided work remains a protocol requirement, not identity verification. Offline grader compares values outside the candidate container and does not trust candidate pass claims.
